gen.prompt:
A documentary film still. Wide shot, eye level, camera slightly off-centre, locked off: the main waiting hall of a provincial European government ministry that has not been renovated since 1974, looking down the length of the hall toward the service counter.

The room: board-marked concrete walls painted institutional mint green up to shoulder height and dirty cream above, the paint scuffed and chipped where chair backs have hit it for fifty years. Grey and white terrazzo floor with brass divider strips, worn dull along the path to the counter. Four rows of moulded mustard-yellow fibreglass chairs bolted to steel beams, one chair cracked. At the far end a long brown wood-veneer counter with six service windows of reeded frosted glass, each with a small round speaking grille and a slot for papers, and a small mechanical number box above each window. High on the end wall a large mechanical split-flap "now serving" board. A red ticket dispenser on a chrome pole near the entrance. A rubber plant in a pot, half dead. A plain wall clock. Tall steel-framed windows on the left with yellowed net curtains. Ceiling of fluorescent tube fittings, two tubes dead. Nearly empty: an old man asleep upright in the third row, a woman knitting at the end of a row.

Photographic qualities: available light only, flat overcast daylight from the windows mixed with greenish fluorescent light, low contrast, soft shadows, deep focus so the whole room is sharp, slight lens vignetting, fine film grain, muted desaturated colour. A real location that has been used every day for decades: dust, wear, mismatched repairs. Shot on an ARRI Alexa with a 32 mm prime. The deadpan tableau framing of Roy Andersson.

Avoid: readable text, signage or logos anywhere; LED screens; blue government signage; glossy or polished surfaces; god rays, haze or dramatic light; rim light; shallow depth of field or bokeh; teal-and-orange grade; HDR look; anything new or clean.

qa.note: Plate candidate. Most photographic: worn terrazzo, chipped mint paint, reeded glass windows, red ticket dispenser, overcast plus fluorescent light. Fix: the board shows a readable 'now serving' label; digits only.

gen.prompt:
A frame from a 1990s European documentary, shot on 35 mm film. Wide frontal tableau at standing eye height, tripod locked off at the entrance end of the room, looking straight down the central aisle at the service counter on the far wall. The camera is square to the far wall, in one-point perspective, a 25 mm lens at f/8.

The place: the main waiting hall of a district government office in a provincial European town. It was built in 1974, still opens every weekday, and has been repainted many times without ever being renovated.

From near to far:
- Lower edge of frame: the backs of the last row of chairs.
- Four rows of moulded mustard-yellow fibreglass shell chairs on black steel beams, in two banks of seven with a two-metre central aisle, all facing the counter. The front row, nearest the counter, is empty.
- Floor: grey and white terrazzo with thin brass divider strips, dull and worn pale along the aisle.
- Walls: chalky institutional mint-green oil paint to shoulder height, then cream yellowed by fifty years of cigarette smoke, scuffed at chair-back height.
- Left wall: three tall steel-framed windows hung with yellowed net curtains, and a tired rubber plant in a clay pot beside the nearest window.
- Right wall: a plain round wall clock, a cast-iron radiator under it and, near the counter, a plain door painted the same green.
- Ceiling: rows of plain fluorescent tube fittings, one tube dark.

The far wall: a long counter in brown teak-effect veneer with six identical service windows. Each window has reeded frosted glass on its lower half and clear glass above, a small round chrome speaking grille at face height, and a brass paper slot at counter height. Five windows are dark, with a beige blind pulled down behind the glass. The fourth window from the left is lit from inside: a middle-aged clerk sits behind it at a desk with a beige fax machine, looking down at her papers. Above each window is a small black box with a single white numeral, 1 to 6 from left to right. Centred high above the counter hangs a large black mechanical split-flap board showing two white digits: 17.

Waiting people, sitting perfectly still:
- In the last row, in the right bank near camera, an old man in a grey overcoat is asleep upright, chin on his chest, his white beard grown long and untrimmed.
- In the second row from the back, in the left bank, a woman in a brown wool coat is knitting. Her scarf is already long enough to run off her lap and along the floor under the chairs.

The light: flat, even, overcast daylight from the windows on the left, mixed with the faintly green cast of the fluorescent tubes. Shadows are soft and grey, pooling under the chairs. Every surface is matte and worn. Everything from the nearest chair to the far wall is in focus. Colour is muted and natural: greyish mint, faded mustard, brown veneer and cool daylight. The image has fine film grain, a slight vignette and the soft, imperfect rendering of an old lens. The only text in the room is the digits on the boxes and the board.
